title: feat(cli,spec): gate the whole declared surface for i18n; translate inline object actions (#3370)
body:
Closes #3370. Framework half of objectstack-ai/objectui#2762 P0-3.

## The problem

In a zh-CN workspace the platform chrome is localized, but author-declared labels leak English — the approval drawer renders **Approve / Reject / Reassign** right next to the inbox's own **通过 / 拒绝**. Two independent holes let that ship.

## 1. The lint gate could not see declared action labels

`os lint`'s i18n coverage kept its **own** walk of the metadata, separate from the walker `os i18n extract` uses to scaffold bundles. The two had drifted: coverage only ever walked the *top-level* `actions` array, while `sys_approval_request` declares its decision actions **inline on the object** (`sys-approval-request.object.ts:250`). Those labels were extractable but ungated — an untranslated one could ship and no lint run would notice.

Coverage now derives its expected keys from `collectExpectedEntries()`, the extractor's walker, so the gated surface and the scaffolded surface cannot disagree again. Newly gated as a result:

- inline object `actions` (label / confirmText / successMessage)
- action `params` (label / helpText / placeholder / options) and `resultDialog` copy
- object-nested `listViews` — label, description, `emptyState`
- object `description`, field `help` / `placeholder`
- the `apps` / `dashboards` / `pages` surfaces

Entries now carry two distinct axes, because they answer different questions: `sourceValue` is what extract seeds the skeleton with (may be a derived fallback like an object's own name), while `inline` is what the reader actually sees — so a string nobody authored is never reported as an untranslated one. **Extract output is byte-identical**, verified by diffing a full `--dry-run` against the committed plugin bundles.

## 2. It has to stay silent for projects that do not translate

This is the constraint that shaped the design: a customer metadata project with no i18n must report **zero** issues, without having to pass `--skip-i18n`.

Which locales get checked is now the project's declaration, never an assumption. `os lint`, `os i18n check` and `os i18n extract` read the stack's own `i18n.defaultLocale` / `i18n.supportedLocales` (already in the schema at `stack.zod.ts:180`, previously ignored by all three), falling back to the locales a bundle already covers, then to `en`. A project declaring neither is checked against its default locale alone — which its inline labels already satisfy.

That also fixes a monolingual **non-English** project being told it owed `en` translations it never claimed to speak: `--default-locale` no longer hardcodes `en` over the config.

Measured on the bundled examples — **0 errors before, 0 errors after**; the deltas are warnings for the newly-visible surface:

| example | i18n issues before | after |
|---|---|---|
| app-crm | 64 | 97 |
| app-todo | 126 | 212 |
| app-showcase | 252 | 456 |

`--i18n-strict` remains the hard CI gate that promotes those to errors.

## 3. The server sent English regardless of locale

`translateObject` walked an object's `label` / `pluralLabel` / `description` / `fields` but never its inline `actions`, so `GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name` returned the authored English literals — even though `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` already ships `_actions` translations for all eight decision actions in zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES. The Console compensated by re-resolving labels client-side against a separately fetched bundle; every other consumer (mobile, plain HTTP, SDUI) rendered the source language. Inline actions now run through the existing `translateAction`, without stamping a synthetic `objectName` onto the response.

## On the issue's second checkbox

"Ship translation bundles for plugin-declared actions" was **already done** — all eight `approval_*` actions have label/confirmText/successMessage/params entries in en, zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES, loaded at `kernel:ready`. The bundles were never the missing piece; nothing consumed them on the wire, and nothing gated them at build time. Both are fixed here.

## New flag: `--no-metadata-forms`

`plugin-approvals`' `os i18n extract --check` was failing because every run emitted `<locale>.metadata-forms.generated.ts`, and that package deliberately commits no such file — the Studio metadata-form baseline is registry-driven and identical for every stack, so exactly one package (`platform-objects`) should own it rather than each plugin carrying a copy.

Worth recording how the first attempt at this went wrong, because the failure mode is the interesting part. Deriving the emission from `--objects-only` looked right and was not: that flag defaults to `true`, so the repo's own `pnpm check:i18n` quietly went from verifying **8 bundles to 4** — the 803-key baseline stopped being drift-checked in all four locales — while still printing a green tick. Caught by running the real CI command against the pre-change file:

```
PRE-CHANGE  → ✓ 8 bundle(s) are in sync
DERIVED     → ✓ 4 bundle(s) are in sync     ← half the coverage, same green tick
```

The two questions are orthogonal: `--objects-only` picks the sub-tree of the *objects* module; `--metadata-forms` (new, defaults to on) decides whether the companion module is written at all. `packages/cli/test/i18n-extract-emitted-files.test.ts` now pins the emit set to the flags, since a file leaving the emit set leaves the drift gate with no other visible symptom.

## Tests

`packages/cli/test/i18n-declared-surface-gate.test.ts` (11 cases) leads with the zero-noise contract, then locks the declared-action gate, the config-driven locale selection, and the extract↔coverage parity. `i18n-extract-emitted-files.test.ts` (4 cases) pins the emit set. Six new resolver cases cover inline-action translation, literal fallback, no synthetic `objectName`, and input immutability.

Suites green after merging `main` (9 commits, no conflicts): spec 6723, cli 662, rest 408, runtime 655, plugin-approvals 239. ESLint clean. `pnpm check:i18n` back to 8 bundles in sync.

## Follow-up filed

#3762 — `platform-objects` declares **55 inline actions across 12 objects** (`Invite User`, `Ban User`, `Unlock Account`, …) with no `objects` translation bundle at all. Same leak, wider, and now visible to the gate this PR adds.
